rows.etymology: 10250 mū́la (mū́ra- AV.) n. 'root' RV., mūlaka- 'arising from' MBh., m.n. 'radish' Mn., mūlikā- f. 'root used in magic' Pañcat. 2. *mūḍa-. [Despite early occurrence and proposed connexion with Gk. μω̑λυ (IEW 750), variation of -l/r- ~ -ḍ- supports non-Aryan, perh. Drav., origin: cf. Tam. muḷā, muḷḷaṅki 'radish' &c., DED 4105. Prob. only chance resemblance with L. and Bi. forms of MIA. muḍḍha- < mūrdhán- with meaning of 'root']
